result.title: Confidence-Based Adaptive Retrieval Fails Where It Matters Most: A Paradox in Biomedical Question Answering
result.summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used for biomedical question answering, but plausible incorrect answers remain a safety risk in clinical settings. Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) can ground responses in medical literature, while confidence-based adaptive RAG retrieves only when the model appears uncertain. We evaluate this routing strategy on three biomedical QA benchmarks of increasing difficulty and compare models across a broad range of parameter scales. The results reveal a paradox: confidence is well calibrated (AUROC 0.78--0.89) on standard medical exam questions where retrieval adds little value (+2.4\% to -1.4\%), yet becomes \emph{near-random} (AUROC 0.506) on specialist-level questions where retrieval helps most (+11.2\%). Five uncertainty signals---first-token probability, margin, entropy, consistency-based sampling, and verbalized confidence---show the same failure pattern. Five post-hoc calibration correction strategies, including density-ratio reweighting and rank-preserving transformation, do not recover a useful routing signal on hard questions (best AUROC: 0.507). Cross-model comparison shows that larger parameter scale and higher base accuracy do not guarantee reliable confidence-based routing under specialist-domain difficulty shift. These findings challenge the premise of confidence-based adaptive RAG: in high-stakes biomedical settings, defaulting to always-retrieve is safer and more accurate than confidence-based routing when calibration on the target domain is unknown.

AI.brief_summary: 在三个难度递增的生物医学 QA 基准上评估「仅当模型不确定时才检索」的置信度自适应 RAG 路由，覆盖多种参数规模与五种不确定性信号、五种事后校准修正，发现置信度在简单考题上校准良好但检索收益有限，在专家级难题上接近随机（AUROC 0.506）而检索收益最大。
AI.relevance_reason: 「置信度门控何时检索」与 LVR 中「何时 LOOK、是否追加视觉证据」的决策机制同构，其「难题上自评信号失效、修正无效」的结论可供核查 latent 自评与停止信号是否也存在同样的难度偏移与校准陷阱。
